stations.name: District SIS
stations.tech: Skyward, PowerSchool, MISTAR-Q, Infinite Campus, Synergy
stations.does: The district's source of truth. Teachers and registrars make the changes.

stations.name: MiDataHub
stations.does: The state clearinghouse. Stamps every record with a change number and keeps a list of deletes.

stations.name: MiGDL Bronze Layer
stations.does: Every package logged exactly as received. Nothing is ever edited here.
stations.note: The last station where the full truth exists.

stations.name: MiGDL Silver Layer
stations.does: One cabinet per district. Files are kept current; history is kept for people and relationships.

stations.name: MiGDL Gold Layer
stations.does: 5a merges all 149 districts into one statewide copy, ~350 shared tables. 5b builds the MiGDL model from 5a: one identity per student, dedup, ISD and district hierarchy.

stations.name: MiGDL Platinum Layer
stations.does: Pre-built views per application: rosters, early-warning metrics, MiRead context.

stations.name: Delivery Counter
stations.tech: MiGDL API and QuickSight + the four Cove apps
stations.does: Where the Cove apps receive the data, protected by the auth handler and district allow-list.

pains.head: No MiGDL pain point at this station.
pains.body: Data quality issues here belong to the district and SIS vendor.

pains.head: We do not know when a district's changes arrive, or how fast we are allowed to pull them.
pains.body: Each district sends its changes to MiDataHub on its own schedule, and nobody has written down when. MiDataHub also limits how fast we can pull, but the limit is not documented, so the nightly run is planned blind. The connector also cannot tell which kinds of records actually changed, so it asks for everything.

pains.head: Nothing is lost here.
pains.asks: Captures inserts, updates, deletes and key changes for every district.
pains.body: Every new record, correction, deletion and ID change from every district is written down exactly as it arrived. This is the last station where the full truth exists.

pains.head: Deleted records never leave (“zombie rows”).
pains.body: A delete arrives in Silver carrying only the record's ID and none of the details, so no fingerprint can be built and nothing is found to remove. The record stays, and everything downstream keeps it too:

pains.head: Address or contact-only changes never make it past Silver.
pains.body: Change detection looks at the student's main record only, not the details attached to it.

pains.head: Corrections are silently thrown away.
pains.body: Once Gold has a record, 47 kinds of record types (attendance, grades, discipline, assessments and most reference data) can never be changed again, only added to. A corrected grade or attendance mark is quietly skipped because a record with that key already exists.

pains.head: When a student's ID is corrected, the system keeps both the old and the new student.
pains.body: An ID correction arrives as a new record instead of replacing the old record. Separately, when a record's history is updated, the old version is closed in one step and the new one written in another; if the run fails in between, the student has no current record at all.

pains.head: One shared warehouse, one checkout line.
pains.body: All 149 districts write into one shared warehouse and wait their turn, and each one re-does all of its work every night even when nothing changed. One small district took About 65 districts fit in a night; we need 79 today and 150 to 175 by fall. Adding computing power did not help.

pains.head: App shelves only add, never fix or remove.
pains.body: Derived and Platinum are built from Gold, and they only ever add rows. A corrected or deleted record upstream leaves the shelf copy untouched, so over time the apps drift away from the data they were built from, even where Gold is right.

pains.head: Apps and the pipeline share the same warehouse.
pains.body: When a teacher opens MiEWIMS while districts are still loading, the app's request waits behind the load and gives up.

pains.head: The tracking system is manual and unreliable.
pains.body: Loads are started by hand, on no fixed schedule. Progress is tracked in a shared spreadsheet that overwrites itself and matches districts by name. A batch reports success as soon as one district finishes, the check that Gold is ready to run is switched off, and there is no record of what any run actually applied.

fixes.head: Find out how much we can pull, then plan the night around it.
fixes.body: Document ODS and DataHub throttling and push cadence; chunk large historical pulls with start and end keys.

fixes.head: Tag every record, match on the Ed-Fi ID.
fixes.body: Tag every Silver record as new, updated, deleted or ID-changed, the same way Bronze does; look deletes up by the Ed-Fi ID. Then re-run the deletes that were missed.

fixes.head: A child change wakes up the parent.
fixes.body: When an address or contact changes, update the student's main record too, so the change gets noticed and travels forward. Then go back and do the same for changes already missed.

fixes.head: Corrections replace the old record instead of being skipped.
fixes.body: Two Gold load paths: MERGE for simple entities; tree replace (close the old parent and children set, insert the new) for record types with children. Pilot first, then rollout. The descriptor loader already proves MERGE in production.

fixes.head: Let deletes reach Gold, then remove what should already be gone.
fixes.body: Pass Silver's delete markers on to Gold, tag Gold records the same way, apply the deletes, remove duplicates, then a one-time clean-up of records that should already be gone.

fixes.head: Run districts in batches, not one by one.
fixes.body: Run Gold and Platinum as separate steps so Platinum only starts once Gold is done; load districts in groups instead of one at a time. The shared vocabulary step already went from 45 minutes per district to one pass for all. Longer term: move the heavy processing out of the shared warehouse.

fixes.head: Every shelf gets refreshed, not just restocked.
fixes.body: Each Platinum table picks one approach: rebuild from scratch each night, or update just the rows that changed. A shared step works out which rows changed upstream and drives the refresh or removal. Wave 1 is the EWIMS and API tables.

fixes.head: Give the apps their own delivery door.
fixes.body: A new, separate store (DynamoDB) just for the apps. After each district finishes loading, a publish step copies app-ready data across; the apps' lookups switch to the new store, with the old ones kept as a fallback. Three production waves.

fixes.head: A real status board: which districts loaded, which did not, and why.
fixes.body: Scheduled orchestration with real readiness gates, a tracker that is not a shared CSV, per-district success reporting, and a queryable record of what each run applied.
fixes.epic: Transferred to MAISA Operations with Cloudwick

decisions.head: How much history does the Gold layer keep?
decisions.body: Today the lake treats 16 record types as “never changes” and 34 as “just overwrite.” A review of all 81 record types found that every one of them does change, and 74 of 81 could be needed for time travel. MAISA needs to confirm the assumption before the resolution proceeds.

decisions.head: Do the app shelves need to answer “what did we know on a given date?”
decisions.body: Nine app-facing tables were built to keep history but never close out old versions.

jobs.name: Amorphic Ed-Fi connector
jobs.does: Pulls by ChangeVersion plus the deletes list; marks the tracker RUNNING - BRONZE LOAD COMPLETED.

jobs.name: maisa_edfi_gold_descriptors_masterdata
jobs.does: 317 descriptors straight from Bronze into gold.edfi_gold_alldescriptors_masterdata, skipping Silver. One native MERGE per district-year. Must finish before Silver and Gold.

jobs.name: edfi_bronze_to_silver
jobs.does: Classifies IU / D / KeyChange, explodes child arrays (244 child and 28 grandchild tables), SCD2 merge into the district's Iceberg tables.

jobs.name: edfi_silver_to_gold_and_platinum
jobs.does: Gold main (81 entities), then Gold derived, then the 24 Platinum statements. Rerun a phase alone with EXECUTE_MODE main, derived, only_platinum or all.

jobs.name: maisa_silver_staging_etl_workflow
jobs.does: Chains the three steps; each waits for the one before, stops at first failure, emails on success and failure. Schedule: edfi_data_curation_schedule.

callouts.head: The only door into the source
callouts.body: Every byte MiGDL holds enters through this one Lambda. It runs under a 15-minute ceiling against rate limits nobody has documented, and it cannot tell which endpoints actually carry deltas. AWS can scale everything to the right of this arrow; this arrow sets the pace.
callouts.fix: Epic 4 (Ingestion at Scale). Tiger Team 1. Not yet in Jira.

callouts.head: Where deletes and ID changes get lost
callouts.body: The job matches rows on lakeid, a hash rebuilt from the record's key columns. A delete arrives carrying only the Ed-Fi id and empty key columns, so the hash cannot be built and nothing matches. One cause, three symptoms: deletes no-op, key changes duplicate, key-changing corrections duplicate.
callouts.fix: G1, match on the Ed-Fi id too (MIGDL-118, 280). Building.

callouts.head: 149 cabinets, one checkout line
callouts.body: Left of this arrow every district has its own tables and runs in parallel. Right of it, all 149 write the same ~350 Redshift tables under table locks and one commit queue, 200 to 350 commits each. Redshift locks whole tables, every statement auto-commits into one serialized queue, and all 81 entities run whether or not anything changed — so the cost is per district and fixed, and does not shrink as nightly change volume shrinks.
callouts.fix: Epic 2 (district groups, split jobs); Epic 3 long term. Partly done.

district-sis.full: The district's own system. Teachers and registrars make the changes.

delta.U: Corrections are routine (e.g. a grade is changed, an absence marked excused).
delta.D: A record is removed at the source (e.g. a dropped class, an enrolment entered in error).
delta.K: A record's identity changes (e.g. an Ed-Fi id or natural-key field is corrected).

midatahub.full: Full history for the district and year requested.

delta.I: Sent as IU rows with content hash and ChangeVersion number.
delta.U: A correction record is re-sent under the same Ed-Fi id with a new hash.
delta.D: Tombstone on the deletes endpoint; carries the Ed-Fi id.
delta.K: Key-change events, carrying old and new key.

bronze.full: The Ed-Fi connector pulls everything. Large pulls hit the 15-minute Lambda limit and need chunking.

delta.I: Landed as recordflag IU with the hash, exactly as received.
delta.U: Every version is kept; nothing is overwritten.
delta.D: Landed as recordflag D with the Ed-Fi id.
delta.K: Landed with old and new keys. Captured, but nothing downstream reads it yet.

bronze.note: The last station where the full package exists.

silver.full: Runs per district in parallel. No shared write targets, so 50 to 100+ districts at once is possible.

delta.I: Applied to the district's Iceberg tables.
delta.U: Applied, unless only a child record changed (e.g. address, contact); those never enter the delta feed.
delta.D: The code path exists (currentflag false by lakeid, cascaded to children) but never fires: the tombstone carries no natural keys.
delta.K: Detected and set aside, not processed in this version (runbook 7.2.6); the new key then lands as a second row beside the original.

gold.full: 5a one district at a time, single file, after hours, 15-minute gap between districts, roughly 50 per night. 5b runs after 5a for the same district; 40 more SQL files.

delta.I: Added if the key is new.
delta.U: 50 entities (G3 scopes 47, excludes 3) have no UPDATE or MERGE, so changed rows are skipped; 31 SCD2 entities expire and re-insert in two separate statement commits (CR-6).
delta.D: Zero DELETE or MERGE statements across the 117 Gold Main load files. Even a corrected Silver could not delete here today.
delta.K: The duplicate and the stranded original both flow through. Gold Derived is accrete-only on top of that.

platinum.full: Same single-file line as Gold. Runs once for all districts, not per district: 24 SQL statements build the app tables (Runbook v1.0).

delta.I: New keys are admitted to the app marts.
delta.U: Not applied, apart from narrow and inconsistent exceptions. The shelf keeps whichever version landed first.
delta.D: Not applied; the student stays on the roster.
delta.K: Two rows for one student. Drifts from Gold even where Gold is right.

delivery.full: District appears in the Cove apps the next morning, if the whole chain finished.

delta.U: The API serves the stale row; QuickSight after the next SPICE refresh.
delta.D: The API serves the zombie row.
delta.K: Both rows served. DDB publish diffs against DynamoDB, not ChangeVersion, so this carries forward until upstream is fixed.
